name: arch_uprobe_get_xol_area
prose: Weak default implementation; it uses current->mm through get_unmapped_area and its caller (xol_add_vma) holds the mmap write lock, but the function itself takes no locks. Postcondition: returns the result of get_unmapped_area(NULL, TASK_SIZE - PAGE_SIZE, PAGE_SIZE, 0, 0): on success a page-aligned, currently unmapped address hint below TASK_SIZE (a hint only, no mapping is created, no address is reserved, and no locks, references or memory are acquired or released), or on failure a negative errno encoded as an unsigned long error code (IS_ERR_VALUE, i.e. result >= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFF001, the range [-4095, -1] as a signed value).
note: Read uprobes.c:1697-1701 and xol_add_vma (1704-1715, mmap_write_lock_killable). Reviewer round-15 claim (not callable in any context: uses current->mm, called under mmap_lock) is RIGHT; the 'any context' wording removed. The return value is get_unmapped_area's result as the prose says.

name: uprobe_copy_process
prose: Precondition: called from copy_process for the not-yet-running new task t while current is the forking parent. Postcondition: t->utask is set to NULL first; if the parent has no utask or no return_instances, or if mm == t->mm and CLONE_VFORK is not set in flags, the function returns with t->utask NULL; otherwise it calls dup_utask, and if that fails it emits a 'dup ret instances' warning and returns with t->utask either NULL (when alloc_utask failed) or non-NULL holding a partially duplicated return_instances list (when a later dup_return_instance failed); if dup_utask succeeds, t->utask holds a duplicate of the parent's return_instances list with depth equal to the number of copied entries and each copied hprobe stable with a refcounted uprobe or NULL, then if the parent mm has no xol_area it emits a 'dup xol area' warning and returns with t->utask set and no xol work queued; if mm == t->mm it returns with t->utask set and no xol work queued; otherwise it sets t->utask->dup_xol_addr to area->vaddr and queues dup_xol_work on t with task_work_add, ignoring task_work_add's return value.
note: Read uprobes.c:2112-2215 (dup_utask, dup_return_instance, uprobe_copy_process). Reviewer claims all RIGHT and in prose: alloc_utask failure returns -ENOMEM with t->utask still NULL (2139-2141); a dup_return_instance failure returns -ENOMEM with t->utask already set (2142, 2149-2151); missing xol_area and same-mm vfork cases return with t->utask set and no work queued; task_work_add result ignored (2214).

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE1(exit, int, error_code)
prose: Generated system call entry for exit(error_code) defined at exit.c:1091-1094. It calls do_exit((error_code & 0xff) << 8); do_exit is declared __noreturn, so control does not come back to the caller and the function returns no value. The exit status passed is the low 8 bits of error_code shifted left by 8.
note: Macro-generated syscall wrapper, named by the SYSCALL_DEFINE1 head per rule 5 (packet name __sys_exit). Read exit.c:1091-1094; the claim 'never returns' rests on do_exit being __noreturn.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE1(exit_group, int, error_code)
prose: Generated system call entry for exit_group(error_code) defined at exit.c:1135-1139. It calls do_group_exit((error_code & 0xff) << 8). do_group_exit uses that code only if no group exit is already in progress and no group exec is in progress (in which case it uses the recorded group_exit_code, or 0 for a group exec task); otherwise it records the code, sets SIGNAL_GROUP_EXIT, kills the other threads under siglock and then calls do_exit. do_group_exit is __noreturn, so the trailing return 0 in the syscall body is not reached.
note: Macro-generated syscall wrapper, named by the SYSCALL_DEFINE1 head per rule 5 (packet name __sys_exit_group). Read exit.c:1100-1139. Added the do_group_exit behaviour with the already-exiting / exec cases the old prose omitted.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE5(waitid, int, which, pid_t, upid, struct siginfo __user *,
prose: Generated function __do_sys_waitid(which, upid, infop, options, ru). Precondition: which is P_ALL, P_PID, P_PGID or P_PIDFD (any other value gives -EINVAL, as does an options value with none of WEXITED, WSTOPPED, WCONTINUED), options contains only WEXITED, WSTOPPED, WCONTINUED, WNOHANG, WNOWAIT, __WNOTHREAD, __WCLONE and __WALL bits, and infop and ru, when non-NULL, point to writable user memory of at least sizeof(struct siginfo) and sizeof(struct rusage) respectively. Postcondition: returns 0 when a child was reported (with the child's rusage copied to *ru when ru is non-NULL and si_signo SIGCHLD, si_errno 0, si_code, si_pid, si_uid and si_status written to *infop when infop is non-NULL) or when WNOHANG was given and no child is ready, or returns a negative error from kernel_waitid (-EINVAL for a bad which or option bits, -ESRCH when no matching child exists, -ECHILD when there is no waitable child, -EINTR when interrupted by a signal, -EAGAIN only when the caller did not pass WNOHANG but the kernel set it because the target is an O_NONBLOCK pidfd (P_PIDFD) and no child is ready) or -EFAULT when the rusage copy or the siginfo write to user memory faults; except when the rusage copy fails or user write access to infop cannot be established, *infop is written even on error paths (with si_signo 0 and zeroed fields).
note: Read exit.c:1745-1851. Prose kept except: P_PIDFD is also a valid 'which', at least one of WEXITED/WSTOPPED/WCONTINUED is required (1754-1755), and -EAGAIN arises only from the pidfd O_NONBLOCK case (1797-1798, 1814-1815). Rule 5 name: macro invocation per rule.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE4(wait4, pid_t, upid, int __user *, stat_addr,
prose: Generated function __do_sys_wait4(upid, stat_addr, options, ru). Precondition: stat_addr is NULL or points to a writable user int, and ru is NULL or points to a writable user buffer of at least sizeof(struct rusage). Postcondition: returns the result of kernel_wait4 — a positive pid of a reaped child (with its status stored to *stat_addr when stat_addr is non-NULL), 0 when WNOHANG was given and no child is ready, or a negative error (-EINVAL for bad option bits, -ESRCH for upid INT_MIN, -ECHILD when there is no waitable child, -EINTR/-ERESTARTSYS when interrupted, -EFAULT when the status store fails) — except that when the return is positive and ru is non-NULL the child's rusage is copied to *ru and a copy failure changes the return to -EFAULT.
note: Read exit.c:1854-1895 and 1913-1924: kernel_wait4 -EINVAL for bad options, -ESRCH for INT_MIN, status store -EFAULT; rusage copy failure -EFAULT when err > 0. Prose correct, kept.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(waitpid, pid_t, pid, int __user *, stat_addr, int, options)
prose: Generated function __do_sys_waitpid(pid, stat_addr, options). Precondition: stat_addr is NULL or points to a writable user int. Postcondition: returns the result of kernel_wait4 with no rusage — a positive pid of a reaped child (with its status stored to *stat_addr when stat_addr is non-NULL), 0 when WNOHANG was given and no child is ready, or a negative error (-EINVAL for bad option bits, -ESRCH for pid INT_MIN, -ECHILD when there is no waitable child, -EINTR/-ERESTARTSYS when interrupted, -EFAULT when the status store fails).
note: Read exit.c:1932-1935 (compiled only with __ARCH_WANT_SYS_WAITPID): returns kernel_wait4(pid, stat_addr, options, NULL). Prose correct, kept.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE4(wait4,
prose: Generated function __do_compat_sys_wait4(pid, stat_addr, options, ru). Precondition: stat_addr is NULL or points to a writable user compat_uint_t, and ru is NULL or points to a writable user buffer of at least sizeof(struct compat_rusage). Postcondition: returns the result of kernel_wait4 — a positive pid of a reaped child (with its status stored to *stat_addr when stat_addr is non-NULL), 0 when WNOHANG was given and no child is ready, or a negative error (-EINVAL for bad option bits, -ESRCH for pid INT_MIN, -ECHILD when there is no waitable child, -EINTR/-ERESTARTSYS when interrupted, -EFAULT when the status store fails) — except that when the return is positive and ru is non-NULL the child's rusage is converted and copied to *ru and a conversion/copy failure changes the return to -EFAULT.
note: Read exit.c:1940-1953 (CONFIG_COMPAT): kernel_wait4 then put_compat_rusage on err > 0, failure -EFAULT. Prose correct, kept.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE5(waitid,
prose: Generated function __do_compat_sys_waitid(which, pid, infop, options, uru). Precondition: which is P_ALL, P_PID, P_PGID or P_PIDFD (any other value gives -EINVAL, as does an options value with none of WEXITED, WSTOPPED, WCONTINUED), options contains only WEXITED, WSTOPPED, WCONTINUED, WNOHANG, WNOWAIT, __WNOTHREAD, __WCLONE and __WALL bits, and infop and uru, when non-NULL, point to writable user memory of at least sizeof(struct compat_siginfo) and sizeof(struct compat_rusage) respectively. Postcondition: returns 0 when a child was reported (with the child's rusage converted and copied to *uru when uru is non-NULL and si_signo SIGCHLD, si_errno 0, si_code, si_pid, si_uid and si_status written to *infop when infop is non-NULL) or when WNOHANG was given and no child is ready, or returns a negative error from kernel_waitid (-EINVAL for a bad which or option bits, -ESRCH when no matching child exists, -ECHILD when there is no waitable child, -EINTR when interrupted by a signal, -EAGAIN only when the caller did not pass WNOHANG but the kernel set it because the target is an O_NONBLOCK pidfd (P_PIDFD) and no child is ready) or -EFAULT when the rusage conversion/copy or the siginfo write to user memory faults; except when the rusage copy fails or user write access to infop cannot be established, *infop is written even on error paths (with si_signo 0 and zeroed fields).
note: Read exit.c:1955-1995. Same corrections as the native waitid (P_PIDFD, required WEXITED/WSTOPPED/WCONTINUED, -EAGAIN only for O_NONBLOCK pidfd). Compat rusage copy: copy_to_user when COMPAT_USE_64BIT_TIME else put_compat_rusage; either failure returns -EFAULT before infop is written.

name: get_futex_key
prose: Precondition: the caller passes a user address uaddr, futex flags, the current process's mm, an access mode rw (FUTEX_READ or FUTEX_WRITE) and a writable union futex_key at key, and holds no page or folio reference that this function consumes. Postcondition: it returns 0 with *key filled in to identify the futex object (mm and address for private futexes, mm sequence number and address for shared anonymous futexes, inode sequence number and page offset for shared file-backed futexes) and retains no page or folio reference, every reference from get_user_pages_fast being dropped with folio_put before return; it returns -EINVAL when the address is not naturally aligned to the futex size (doubled for FLAGS_NUMA) or when the NUMA node read from userspace is not FUTEX_NO_NODE and is either >= MAX_NUMNODES or not a possible node; it returns -EFAULT when access_ok fails, when should_fail_futex triggers (before the lookup or in the shared anonymous path), when the NUMA node value cannot be read from or written back to userspace, when the folio's mapping is NULL and the page is not a shmem page swizzled to swapcache (after taking and releasing the folio lock), or when a shared read-only anonymous page is encountered; otherwise it returns the negative error code produced by get_user_pages_fast, and on the retry paths (shmem swizzle, folio->mapping change under RCU, missing mapping->host) it jumps back to the page lookup (get_user_pages_fast and the mapping checks, not the alignment or NUMA handling, which are done once) and returns only with one of the outcomes above.
note: Slice cut the head; real function get_futex_key at futex/core.c:516-738 read in full. Reviewer round-15 claim (goto again re-runs only the page lookup, not the alignment/NUMA steps) is RIGHT (601 label is after 536-576); prose corrected. Private futexes (not FLAGS_SHARED) return at line 598 before any page lookup, covered by the 'mm and address' wording.

name: futex_requeue_pi_wakeup_sync
prose: Precondition: q points to a valid futex_q whose requeue_state field is concurrently modified by the requeue side (futex_requeue_pi_prepare(), reached also from futex_proxy_trylock_atomic(), and futex_requeue_pi_complete()) and by this function. Postcondition: if the state read on entry is Q_REQUEUE_PI_DONE or Q_REQUEUE_PI_LOCKED, it returns that value immediately without modifying the state; otherwise it atomically changes the state from the value old observed by a successful atomic_try_cmpxchg() to Q_REQUEUE_PI_IGNORE when old is Q_REQUEUE_PI_NONE and to Q_REQUEUE_PI_WAIT otherwise, waits until the state is no longer Q_REQUEUE_PI_WAIT only when old is Q_REQUEUE_PI_IN_PROGRESS (sleeping uninterruptibly on PREEMPT_RT and spinning otherwise), and then returns the current state, so the return value is Q_REQUEUE_PI_IGNORE, Q_REQUEUE_PI_WAIT, Q_REQUEUE_PI_DONE or Q_REQUEUE_PI_LOCKED (Q_REQUEUE_PI_WAIT only when old was Q_REQUEUE_PI_IGNORE or Q_REQUEUE_PI_WAIT and the requeue side has not yet completed, Q_REQUEUE_PI_IGNORE when old was Q_REQUEUE_PI_NONE or when a failed requeue moved a waited-on Q_REQUEUE_PI_IN_PROGRESS or Q_REQUEUE_PI_WAIT to Q_REQUEUE_PI_IGNORE, and Q_REQUEUE_PI_DONE/Q_REQUEUE_PI_LOCKED when the requeue completed); it does not acquire or release any lock and does not change the waiter's hash-bucket membership.
note: Read requeue.c:171-207 and 99-168. Reviewer claims: round-1 (WAIT/IGNORE on entry returns WAIT without blocking) RIGHT and in prose; round-2 (can return IGNORE after requeue failure) RIGHT and in prose; round-15 (futex_proxy_trylock_atomic also sets IN_PROGRESS) RIGHT only in that futex_proxy_trylock_atomic calls futex_requeue_pi_prepare (line 330): the precondition now names that path.

name: futex_wait_requeue_pi
prose: Waits on uaddr and may be requeued onto the PI futex uaddr2 (requeue.c:794-925). It returns -ENOSYS if CONFIG_FUTEX_PI is disabled, and -EINVAL if uaddr == uaddr2 or bitset is zero. It sets up an optional timeout (futex_setup_timer), initialises a stack rt_mutex_waiter, resolves the key for uaddr2 with get_futex_key (a non-zero result goes to out) and calls futex_wait_setup (non-zero result goes to out), then sleeps in futex_do_wait. After waking it calls futex_requeue_pi_wakeup_sync and switches on the state. IGNORE (early wakeup before any requeue): under the hash bucket lock it calls handle_early_requeue_pi_wakeup and returns its result. LOCKED (the lock was acquired by the requeuer): if q.pi_state is set and its owner is not current, it takes q.lock_ptr, runs fixup_pi_owner, drops the pi_state and the lock, and sets ret to the error if negative, else 0; otherwise ret is left as initialised by that path. DONE (requeued): it waits for the proxy lock with rt_mutex_wait_proxy_lock; on error it calls rt_mutex_cleanup_proxy_lock and if that reports the lock was acquired it clears ret to 0; it takes q.lock_ptr, calls debug_rt_mutex_free_waiter, runs fixup_pi_owner (a non-zero result replaces ret, a positive one meaning 0), unqueues the pi state and unlocks q.lock_ptr, and converts -EINTR to -EWOULDBLOCK. Any other state is a BUG(). Except on the paths that goto out early, it then calls futex_private_hash_put(q.drop_fph). At out, if a timeout was set up, the hrtimer is cancelled and destroyed. It returns ret (0, or one of the errors above including those propagated from futex_wait_setup, get_futex_key and the proxy-lock wait such as -ETIMEDOUT).
note: Slice cut the head (name outside slice); real function futex_wait_requeue_pi at requeue.c:794-925. Reviewer round-15 claim (rt_waiter is not freed on every path: debug_rt_mutex_free_waiter runs only in the DONE branch) is RIGHT (885); rt_waiter is a stack object and old claims that it is 'freed on every path' and that pi_state and hash references are all dropped on every path are removed.

name: prepare_percpu_nmi
prose: The function expects to be called from non-preemptible context (it only issues WARN_ON(preemptible()) and does not enforce this). Postcondition: it acquires and releases the per-CPU irq descriptor lock for irq; returns -EINVAL if the descriptor cannot be acquired or the per-CPU check fails, or if irq is not an NMI interrupt (with a WARN); otherwise returns the value returned by irq_nmi_setup (0 on success, negative errno on failure, with an error message printed on failure), and the lock is released before returning in every case.
note: Read irq/manage.c:2607-2623. Reviewer round-15 claim (if the descriptor cannot be acquired the body is skipped and the initial value of ret is returned) is RIGHT but the initial value is -EINVAL (line 2609), so the old prose '-EINVAL if the descriptor cannot be acquired' is correct. The non-preemptible condition is only a WARN_ON, wording corrected.

name: __irq_set_trigger
prose: Precondition: desc points to a valid irq descriptor and flags carries IRQF_TRIGGER_* bits, of which only IRQ_TYPE_SENSE_MASK is used. Postcondition: returns 0 without touching the descriptor or hardware when desc->irq_data.chip is NULL or the chip has no irq_set_type callback; otherwise, when the chip has IRQCHIP_SET_TYPE_MASKED it masks the irq if it is not already masked (even when the irq is disabled) and records a pending unmask only if the irq is not disabled, calls chip->irq_set_type with flags reduced to IRQ_TYPE_SENSE_MASK, and on IRQ_SET_MASK_OK, IRQ_SET_MASK_OK_DONE or IRQ_SET_MASK_OK_NOCOPY updates the descriptor's trigger type and level state and returns 0 after unmasking the irq if a pending unmask was recorded, while any other callback return value is logged as an error, the descriptor is left unchanged by that switch, the common unmask step still runs if a pending unmask was recorded, and that return value is returned; no locks or references are held on return.
note: Read irq/manage.c:914-967. Reviewer claims: round-1 (early return 0 when no irq_set_type) RIGHT, in prose; round-2 (masks even when disabled; unmask only if not disabled) RIGHT, in prose; round-15 (the default case does not return immediately, it falls to the unmask step at 964-965) RIGHT; prose corrected. For IRQ_SET_MASK_OK_NOCOPY the trigger bits are not rewritten from flags (948 case), only the cached mask/level state is recomputed.

name: note_interrupt
prose: Accounts for one interrupt's handler result action_ret on descriptor desc and detects stuck interrupts (spurious.c:222-380). It returns immediately with no side effect if IRQS_POLL_INPROGRESS is set or the irq is polled. If action_ret is not a valid irqreturn_t (more than IRQ_HANDLED | IRQ_WAKE_THREAD) it calls report_bad_irq (which logs and dumps the stack, taking desc->lock internally) and returns. If IRQ_WAKE_THREAD is set it uses desc->threads_handled_last / threads_handled: for plain IRQ_WAKE_THREAD the first call just sets SPURIOUS_DEFERRED and returns, later calls upgrade action_ret to IRQ_HANDLED if the thread handled count changed (updating threads_handled_last) or downgrade it to IRQ_NONE if not; for other values with the bit set it clears SPURIOUS_DEFERRED. If action_ret is IRQ_NONE it updates irqs_unhandled (set to 1 if the last unhandled was more than HZ/10 ago, else incremented) and last_unhandled. It then calls try_misrouted_irq and, if that is true, misrouted_irq, subtracting the number of handled misrouted interrupts from irqs_unhandled when action_ret is IRQ_NONE. If irqs_unhandled is zero it returns; otherwise it increments irq_count and returns while irq_count < 100000; when irq_count reaches 100000 it resets it to 0, and if irqs_unhandled > 99900 it reports the bad IRQ (__report_bad_irq), prints "Disabling IRQ", sets IRQS_SPURIOUS_DISABLED, increments depth, calls irq_disable and arms poll_spurious_irq_timer; in that case and otherwise it finally resets irqs_unhandled to 0. It returns no value. Locking: it is called without desc->lock (as the code notes), and takes none directly itself.
note: Slice cut the head; real function note_interrupt at irq/spurious.c:222-380. Reviewer round-15 claim (code has no 'bogus return value returns with no side effect' and acts on bad action_ret) is RIGHT: bad_action_ret leads to report_bad_irq (229-231); polling in progress simply returns (226-227). I could not confirm any clearing of IRQS_POLL_INPROGRESS in this function; that part of the reviewer claim is not supported by the code. Old prose also said irq_count is tested without noting it only increments when irqs_unhandled is nonzero (355-359); corrected.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE5(kcmp, pid_t, pid1, pid_t, pid2, int, type,
prose: Precondition: none beyond the syscall arguments, except that when type is KCMP_EPOLL_TFD the value idx2 is interpreted as a user-space pointer to a readable struct kcmp_epoll_slot. Postcondition: the generated function __do_sys_kcmp looks up pid1 and pid2 in the caller's PID namespace and returns -ESRCH without taking references or locks if either is not found; otherwise it takes task references, acquires read lock(s) on the tasks' exec_update_lock via kcmp_lock (returning -EINTR and releasing any lock already acquired if interrupted), checks ptrace access (returning -EPERM after unlocking and dropping references if denied), and then returns 0, 1 or 2 for the obfuscated comparison selected by type, or -EBADF for a missing file descriptor, -EFAULT for an unreadable epoll slot, -EINVAL for an invalid type, -EOPNOTSUPP for a type not compiled in, or another negative error from the epoll target lookup, with all locks released and task references dropped before return.
note: Read kcmp.c:135-226 and kcmp_lock/unlock (73-95): -ESRCH before any reference (146-149, 223-225), kcmp_lock uses down_read_killable (error, e.g. -EINTR, with any held lock released), ptrace_may_access failure -EPERM, kcmp_ptr returns 0, 1 or 2, -EBADF for missing files in KCMP_FILE (and in the epoll target lookup), -EFAULT for the epoll slot copy, -EINVAL for an unknown type, -EOPNOTSUPP for KCMP_SYSVSEM without SYSVIPC or KCMP_EPOLL_TFD without EPOLL. Round-2 reviewer claim (not both locks on every path) is RIGHT and the prose already states 'acquires read lock(s)' and the interrupted case. Old contract dropped as it only restated the return list.

name: kcov_ioctl_locked
prose: Handles KCOV_ENABLE, KCOV_DISABLE and KCOV_REMOTE_ENABLE for kcov with kcov->lock held by the caller (kcov.c:587-693); any other cmd returns -ENOTTY with no change. For KCOV_REMOTE_ENABLE, arg is a kernel pointer to a struct kcov_remote_arg prepared by kcov_ioctl. KCOV_ENABLE: returns -EINVAL if kcov->mode is not KCOV_MODE_INIT or kcov->area is NULL, -EBUSY if kcov->t or current->kcov is set, or the negative result of kcov_get_mode(arg), with no state change; otherwise it faults in the area, sets kcov->mode, calls kcov_start (sets current->kcov, size, area, sequence and mode), sets kcov->t = current, takes a reference with kcov_get and returns 0. KCOV_DISABLE: returns -EINVAL if arg is non-zero or current->kcov != kcov, or if WARN_ON(kcov->t != current), with no change; otherwise it calls kcov_disable (kcov_task_reset on current, then kcov_reset, or kcov_remote_reset for a remote kcov, which also deletes this kcov's remote entries and clears mode to KCOV_MODE_INIT, remote false, remote_size 0, t NULL, and increments the sequence), then drops one reference with kcov_put and returns 0. KCOV_REMOTE_ENABLE: same -EINVAL/-EBUSY checks as ENABLE, the kcov_get_mode error for remote_arg->trace_mode, and -EINVAL if remote_arg->area_size > LONG_MAX / sizeof(unsigned long), all with no change; otherwise it sets kcov->mode, current->kcov and kcov_mode (KCOV_MODE_REMOTE), kcov->t, kcov->remote and remote_size, then with kcov_remote_lock held validates each handle with kcov_check_handle and registers it with kcov_remote_add, and the common_handle likewise (also setting current->kcov_handle). If any handle is invalid (-EINVAL) or kcov_remote_add fails (its PTR_ERR), it releases kcov_remote_lock and calls kcov_disable(current, kcov), which undoes the setup, including deleting the remote handles already added and resetting kcov->mode to KCOV_MODE_INIT, and returns the error without taking a kcov reference. On success it releases the lock, takes a kcov reference with kcov_get and returns 0.
note: Read kcov.c:395-444 and 587-693. Reviewer claims all RIGHT: round-1 and round-2 (error paths call kcov_disable, which changes state; fields do not remain set) corrected, the old prose wrongly said kcov->mode, remote, remote_size and handles stay set; round-15 (kcov_disable does not drop a reference; kcov_put is explicit in KCOV_DISABLE at 630, remote error paths take none) corrected.

name: DEFINE_MEMORY_BARRIER(mb, true)
prose: Generated function __kcsan_mb(void): the caller must be in a context where get_ctx() yields a valid KCSAN context; it takes no arguments and holds no locks. It returns nothing and acquires or releases no locks or references; if get_reorder_access(get_ctx()) returns NULL nothing is modified, otherwise (order_before_cond is true) the reorder access's size field is set to 0.
note: Read kcsan/core.c:970-984: DEFINE_MEMORY_BARRIER(mb, true) defines __kcsan_mb, which returns if get_reorder_access(get_ctx()) is NULL, else sets sa->size = 0 when the condition holds. Prose correct, kept.

name: DEFINE_MEMORY_BARRIER(wmb, sa->type & (KCSAN_ACCESS_WRITE | KCSAN_ACCESS_COMPOUND))
prose: Generated function __kcsan_wmb(void): the caller must be in a context where get_ctx() yields a valid KCSAN context; it takes no arguments and holds no locks. It returns nothing and acquires or releases no locks or references; if get_reorder_access(get_ctx()) returns NULL nothing is modified, otherwise the reorder access's size field is set to 0 only when its type has KCSAN_ACCESS_WRITE or KCSAN_ACCESS_COMPOUND set, and is left unchanged otherwise.
note: Read kcsan/core.c:970-982: condition is sa->type & (KCSAN_ACCESS_WRITE | KCSAN_ACCESS_COMPOUND). Prose correct, kept.

name: DEFINE_MEMORY_BARRIER(rmb, !(sa->type & KCSAN_ACCESS_WRITE) || (sa->type & KCSAN_ACCESS_COMPOUND))
prose: Generated function __kcsan_rmb(void): the caller must be in a context where get_ctx() yields a valid KCSAN context; it takes no arguments and holds no locks. It returns nothing and acquires or releases no locks or references; if get_reorder_access(get_ctx()) returns NULL nothing is modified, otherwise the reorder access's size field is set to 0 only when its type lacks KCSAN_ACCESS_WRITE or has KCSAN_ACCESS_COMPOUND set, and is left unchanged otherwise.
note: Read kcsan/core.c:970-983: condition is !(sa->type & KCSAN_ACCESS_WRITE) || (sa->type & KCSAN_ACCESS_COMPOUND). Prose correct, kept.

name: DEFINE_MEMORY_BARRIER(release, true)
prose: Generated function __kcsan_release(void): the caller must be in a context where get_ctx() yields a valid KCSAN context; it takes no arguments and holds no locks. It returns nothing and acquires or releases no locks or references; if get_reorder_access(get_ctx()) returns NULL nothing is modified, otherwise (order_before_cond is true) the reorder access's size field is set to 0.
note: Read kcsan/core.c:970-984: DEFINE_MEMORY_BARRIER(release, true); same body as mb. Prose correct, kept.

name: TEST_KERNEL_LOCKED(with_memorder,
prose: Precondition: none; the function attempts to acquire the lock word test_struct.val[0] by compare-exchanging 0 for 1 with acquire semantics (cmpxchg_acquire). Postcondition: if the word held 0, it is set to 1, test_var is incremented 100 times (with a barrier() between iterations), the word is then stored back as 0 with release semantics (smp_store_release), and test_delay(10) is called, which reads test_sink 10 times and writes test_sink; if the word held a nonzero value, the compare-exchange fails and the function returns immediately without modifying test_var or the lock word. The function returns void and takes no parameters.
note: Read kcsan_test.c:492-512: TEST_KERNEL_LOCKED(with_memorder, cmpxchg_acquire(flag, 0, 1) == 0, smp_store_release(flag, 0)) defines test_kernel_with_memorder; if the acquire expression is false the function returns at once; else the 100-iteration test_var++ loop, release, then test_delay(10). Prose correct, kept.

name: TEST_KERNEL_LOCKED(wrong_memorder,
prose: Precondition: none; the function attempts to acquire the lock word test_struct.val[0] by compare-exchanging 0 for 1 with relaxed semantics (cmpxchg_relaxed). Postcondition: if the word held 0, it is set to 1, test_var is incremented 100 times (with a barrier() between iterations), the word is then stored back as 0 with a relaxed WRITE_ONCE(*flag, 0), and test_delay(10) is called, which reads test_sink 10 times and writes test_sink; if the word held a nonzero value, the compare-exchange fails and the function returns immediately without modifying test_var or the lock word. The function returns void and takes no parameters.
note: Read kcsan_test.c:492-512 (wrong_memorder: cmpxchg_relaxed and WRITE_ONCE). Prose correct, kept.

name: TEST_KERNEL_LOCKED(atomic_builtin_with_memorder,
prose: Precondition: none; the function attempts to acquire the lock word test_struct.val[0] with __atomic_compare_exchange_n(flag, &v, 1, 0, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE, __ATOMIC_RELAXED), where the local v starts at 0. Postcondition: if the word held 0, it is set to 1 with acquire semantics, test_var is incremented 100 times (with a barrier() between iterations), the word is then stored back as 0 with an atomic release store (__atomic_store_n(flag, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE)), and test_delay(10) is called, which reads test_sink 10 times and writes test_sink; if the word held a nonzero value, the compare-exchange fails, the local v is updated with the observed value (no effect outside the function), and the function returns immediately without modifying test_var or the lock word. The function returns void and takes no parameters.
note: Read kcsan_test.c:492-516 (atomic_builtin_with_memorder). Note v starts at 0 and is also the loop counter: on success the loop runs while v++ < 100, i.e. 100 iterations; on failure v receives the observed value and the function returns. Prose correct, kept.

name: TEST_KERNEL_LOCKED(atomic_builtin_wrong_memorder,
prose: Precondition: none; the function attempts to acquire the lock word test_struct.val[0] with __atomic_compare_exchange_n(flag, &v, 1, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED, __ATOMIC_RELAXED), where the local v starts at 0. Postcondition: if the word held 0, it is set to 1 with relaxed semantics, test_var is incremented 100 times (with a barrier() between iterations), the word is then stored back as 0 with an atomic relaxed store (__atomic_store_n(flag, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED)), and test_delay(10) is called, which reads test_sink 10 times and writes test_sink; if the word held a nonzero value, the compare-exchange fails, the local v is updated with the observed value (no effect outside the function), and the function returns immediately without modifying test_var or the lock word. The function returns void and takes no parameters.
note: Read kcsan_test.c:492-518 (atomic_builtin_wrong_memorder: relaxed compare-exchange and relaxed store). Prose correct, kept.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE4(kexec_load, compat_ulong_t, entry,
prose: Generated compat system call entry for kexec_load(entry, nr_segments, segments, flags) defined at kexec.c:268-308 (CONFIG_COMPAT). It first returns the non-zero result of kexec_load_check(nr_segments, flags) if that check fails (it covers CAP_SYS_BOOT, the kexec-disabled state, the LSM hook, valid flags and nr_segments <= KEXEC_SEGMENT_MAX; a negative errno). It returns -EINVAL if (flags & KEXEC_ARCH_MASK) == KEXEC_ARCH_DEFAULT, and -ENOMEM if kmalloc_array for the segment array fails. It then copies each of the nr_segments compat_kexec_segment structures from user space with copy_from_user and converts them into kexec_segment entries; if a copy fails it returns copy_from_user's result (the positive number of bytes not copied), not an errno. Otherwise it returns do_kexec_load(entry, nr_segments, ksegments, flags) (0 or a negative errno). After the array has been allocated it is freed with kfree on both the failure and the do_kexec_load paths.
note: Macro-generated compat wrapper, named by the COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE4 head per rule 5 (packet name compat_sys_kexec_load). Read kexec.c:268-308. Old prose put the checks under 'Precondition' although they are returns; the facts about returns were right; reorganised.

name: debug_class_ops_read
prose: Precondition: class points to a lock_class that lies within the lock_classes array, so that class - lock_classes is a valid non-negative index into the per-CPU lockdep_stats.lock_class_ops array. Postcondition: returns the sum, over all possible CPUs, of the per-CPU lockdep_stats.lock_class_ops[class - lock_classes] counters; no locks, references or memory are acquired or released.
note: Read lockdep_internals.h:248-257: sums per_cpu(lockdep_stats.lock_class_ops[idx], cpu) over all possible CPUs, with idx = class - lock_classes. Packet name lockdep_class_ops_sum is not defined; the real function is debug_class_ops_read, compiled only when the debug counters are enabled (the #else branch at 259-265 defines only no-op macros). Prose otherwise correct.

name: alloc_pid
prose: Allocates a struct pid for namespace ns, with one numeric id in each namespace from ns up to the root (pid.c:163-309). set_tid, if set_tid_size is non-zero, supplies requested ids starting from the innermost namespace. It returns ERR_PTR(-EINVAL) at once if set_tid_size > ns->level + 1. It allocates the pid from ns->pid_cachep (ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) on failure) and then for each level, innermost first: with a requested tid it fails with -EINVAL if tid < 1 or tid >= pid_max or if tid != 1 and that namespace has no child_reaper, and with -EPERM if checkpoint_restore_ns_capable fails; ids are allocated under pidmap_lock with idr_alloc (requested tid; -ENOSPC becomes -EEXIST) or idr_alloc_cyclic (no tid); an allocation failure returns -EAGAIN when idr_alloc_cyclic reported -ENOSPC, -EEXIST for an already used requested tid, or the other negative error from idr. After all levels are allocated it takes a reference on ns (get_pid_ns), initialises the pid (count 1, task lists, wait queue), and under pidmap_lock, if PIDNS_ADDING is no longer set in ns->pid_allocated, it fails with -ENOMEM (dropping the ns reference); otherwise it adds the pid to pidfs, installs the pid in each level's idr with idr_replace, increments pid_allocated for each level, and returns the new pid. On every failure path it removes the idr entries already allocated for the inner levels, resets ns's idr cursor to 0 if ns->pid_allocated is exactly PIDNS_ADDING, frees the pid, and returns ERR_PTR of the error.
note: Slice cut the head (name outside slice); real function alloc_pid at pid.c:163-309 read in full. Reviewer round-15 claim (idr_alloc returns -ENOSPC/-ENOMEM, not -EAGAIN) is PARTLY WRONG: -EAGAIN is produced by the function from -ENOSPC at line 245; the old prose omitted -EEXIST (223-224, 245). Also -EPERM and the NS reference handling are now precise.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE2(pidfd_open, pid_t, pid, unsigned int, flags)
prose: Generated system call entry for pidfd_open(pid, flags) defined at pid.c:646-665. It returns -EINVAL, taking no reference, if flags has any bit other than PIDFD_NONBLOCK or PIDFD_THREAD, or if pid <= 0. It looks up the struct pid with find_get_pid in the caller's namespace and returns -ESRCH if there is none. It then calls pidfd_create(p, flags) (which calls pidfd_prepare), drops its struct pid reference with put_pid in every case, and returns pidfd_create's result: a new non-negative O_CLOEXEC file descriptor owned by the caller, or a negative errno: -ESRCH if the pid no longer has a task, -ENOENT if flags lacks PIDFD_THREAD and the pid has no thread-group-leader task, or the error from allocating the descriptor (such as -EMFILE) or the pidfs file (such as -ENFILE or -ENOMEM).
note: Macro-generated syscall wrapper named by the SYSCALL_DEFINE2 head per rule 5. Read pid.c:620-665 and fork.c:1831-1873 (pidfd_prepare). Old prose was WRONG in returning -EINVAL for a non-thread-group-leader without PIDFD_THREAD: pidfd_prepare returns -ENOENT (fork.c:1859-1860); it also omitted the -ESRCH from pidfd_prepare (1852-1853).

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(pidfd_getfd, int, pidfd, int, fd,
prose: Generated system call entry for pidfd_getfd(pidfd, fd, flags) defined at pid.c:876-894, which duplicates descriptor fd of another process into the caller. It returns -EINVAL if flags is non-zero and -EBADF if pidfd is not an open descriptor of the caller. It then takes the struct pid from the pidfd with pidfd_pid, returning its error (-EBADF if the file is not a pidfd), and calls pidfd_getfd, which looks up the task with get_pid_task (-ESRCH if it no longer exists) and calls __pidfd_fget: that takes the target's exec_update_lock for reading with down_read_killable (error such as -EINTR returned), then returns -EPERM if ptrace_may_access(PTRACE_MODE_ATTACH_REALCREDS) fails, -ESRCH if the task is exiting, else fget_task of fd; if no file results it returns -ESRCH when the task is exiting and -EBADF otherwise. The lock and the task reference are released before return. With the file in hand it installs it with receive_fd(file, NULL, O_CLOEXEC), drops its file reference and returns the new non-negative descriptor or the error from receive_fd.
note: Macro-generated syscall wrapper named by the SYSCALL_DEFINE3 head per rule 5 (packet name pidfd_getfd_syscall). Read pid.c:799-894 and pidfd_pid (fs/pidfs.c:617-622). Old prose was WRONG in saying -EINVAL when pidfd does not refer to a pidfd: pidfd_pid returns -EBADF.

name: software_resume
prose: Resumes from a hibernation image (hibernate.c:1037-1113). It takes system_transition_mutex itself and releases it on every return. It calls swsusp_check(true): an error goes to Unlock and is returned. If the image is compressed it selects hib_comp_algo and returns -EOPNOTSUPP (to Unlock) if crypto_has_acomp says that algorithm is unavailable. If hibernate_acquire() fails it returns -EBUSY after swsusp_close(). Otherwise it calls pm_prepare_console and pm_notifier_call_chain_robust(PM_RESTORE_PREPARE, PM_POST_RESTORE); on error it goes to Restore (the robust call has already run PM_POST_RESTORE), where it calls pm_restore_console, prints "resume failed", calls hibernate_release and unlocks. Otherwise it freezes filesystems (filesystems_freeze), then freeze_processes (on error thaws the filesystems and goes to Close_Finish), then freeze_kernel_threads (on error thaw_processes, thaw the filesystems, go to Close_Finish), then load_image_and_restore; after that call returns (normally the restored kernel runs instead) it thaws processes and filesystems and goes to Finish. Close_Finish calls swsusp_close() and goes to Finish; so swsusp_close() is not called on the swsusp_check failure, the compression failure, the notifier failure, or the plain load_image_and_restore return. Finish runs pm_notifier_call_chain(PM_POST_RESTORE) and falls into Restore (console restore, message, hibernate_release) and Unlock. The returned value is the error from whichever step failed, or load_image_and_restore's return value (which is 0 only if it returned 0).
note: Read hibernate.c:1037-1113. Reviewer claims all RIGHT: round-2 (early failures skip console restore, PM_POST_RESTORE and hibernate_release) and round-15 (load_image_and_restore return falls through to Finish without swsusp_close) are reflected; the old prose already had the correct lists but is rewritten as a path list. hibernate_release is only reached on the Finish/Restore paths, not on the three early failures.

name: create_image
prose: Precondition: platform_mode selects whether the platform driver's pre-snapshot/leave/finish callbacks are invoked, and the function is called after dpm_suspend_end has suspended devices. Postcondition: returns 0 on success or a negative error code; if dpm_suspend_end(PMSG_FREEZE) fails, it returns that error immediately without calling platform_finish or dpm_resume_start. On every other path platform_finish(platform_mode) is called and dpm_resume_start is called with PMSG_RECOVER if in_suspend is set and error is nonzero, PMSG_THAW if in_suspend is set and error is zero, or PMSG_RESTORE if in_suspend is clear. syscore_resume is called on every path on which syscore_suspend succeeded (including the wakeup-pending and TEST_CORE exits), but not when syscore_suspend failed (that path goes to Enable_irqs), system_state is set back to SYSTEM_RUNNING and local interrupts re-enabled on every path after local_irq_disable, and secondary CPUs are re-enabled on every path after pm_sleep_disable_secondary_cpus. On the normal path in_suspend is set to 1 before swsusp_arch_suspend; if it is clear when control returns, events_check_enabled is cleared and free pages are cleared or poisoned; platform_leave(platform_mode) is called afterwards whether or not in_suspend is clear. Whenever in_suspend is clear at the Enable_cpus point, error is overwritten with the return value of arch_resume_nosmt().
note: Slice cut the head (name outside slice); real function create_image at hibernate.c:324-393. Reviewer claims: round-1 (dpm_suspend_end failure returns early) RIGHT and in prose; round-2 (syscore_resume skipped / events cleared contradiction) partly RIGHT; round-15 (syscore_resume skipped when syscore_suspend fails, 347-349) RIGHT; also platform_leave is unconditional (370). The error overwrite by arch_resume_nosmt whenever in_suspend is clear (383-384) was already in the prose and is correct (it can overwrite an earlier error, e.g. from pm_sleep_disable_secondary_cpus).

name: freeze_filesystems_store
prose: Precondition: kobj and attr are the sysfs objects for this attribute and buf points to a NUL-terminated string of at least n bytes holding a base-10 unsigned long. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL without touching filesystem_freeze_enabled if kstrtoul fails or the parsed value exceeds 1, and otherwise sets filesystem_freeze_enabled to !!val and returns n.
note: Read power/main.c:999-1013: kstrtoul(buf, 10, &val) failure or val > 1 gives -EINVAL with filesystem_freeze_enabled unchanged; otherwise it stores !!val and returns n. Prose correct, kept.

name: try_to_freeze_tasks
prose: Tries to freeze all freezable tasks (and, when user_only is false, the freezable workqueues) within freeze_timeout_msecs (process.c:28-112). It logs the start and, if user_only is false, calls freeze_workqueues_begin. It then loops: under read_lock(tasklist_lock) it calls freeze_task on every process thread other than current, counting those that are not yet frozen; the lock is released before continuing; for user_only false it adds 1 to the count if freeze_workqueues_busy reports busy workqueues. The loop ends if the count is zero or the timeout has passed; otherwise, if pm_wakeup_pending() it records a wakeup and ends the loop; otherwise it sleeps with usleep_range (up to 8 ms) and rescans. After the loop it logs; if the count is non-zero it prints the tasks (read_lock(tasklist_lock) again) and workqueues still not frozen. It returns -EBUSY if the final count was non-zero (timeout, wakeup abort, or refusing tasks or busy workqueues) and 0 if the final scan found nothing left to freeze. No lock is held on return, and the function may sleep; it relies on the caller (freeze_processes, freeze_kernel_threads) having set pm_freezing or pm_nosig_freezing first.
note: Read process.c:28-112. Old prose said 0 only if every freezable task entered the refrigerator before the timeout elapsed; the code returns 0 whenever the final scan counts nothing left (66-67, 111), even if the timeout also happened to expire. Old contract dropped: Frama-C rejected it and the function reads and writes global state (rule 4).

name: freeze_kernel_threads
prose: In normal use user space has already been frozen by a prior freeze_processes() call (this is not checked) and the caller holds no locks, in particular not tasklist_lock. Postcondition: it returns 0 when all freezable kernel threads and workqueues have entered the refrigerator; it returns -EBUSY (-16) if any of them refuse to freeze or the timeout expires, in which case it has already called thaw_kernel_threads() and the user space tasks remain frozen, so the caller is responsible for thawing them later; no lock is held on return.
note: Read process.c:165-177: sets pm_nosig_freezing = true, calls try_to_freeze_tasks(false), BUG_ON(in_atomic()); on error calls thaw_kernel_threads() and returns the error (-EBUSY). Prose otherwise correct; the precondition is not enforced. Old contract dropped (rejected, and the function touches global state).

name: count_pages_for_highmem
prose: Precondition: nr_highmem is any unsigned int; when CONFIG_HIGHMEM is defined, alloc_highmem is the number of highmem pages already allocated for the image and count_free_highmem_pages() returns the number of currently free highmem pages. Postcondition: when CONFIG_HIGHMEM is defined, if count_free_highmem_pages() + alloc_highmem >= nr_highmem the function returns 0, otherwise it returns nr_highmem - (count_free_highmem_pages() + alloc_highmem), which is positive and at most nr_highmem; when CONFIG_HIGHMEM is not defined, it returns 0 for every nr_highmem; in both cases it allocates no memory, takes no locks and modifies no state.
note: Read snapshot.c:1991-2004 and count_free_highmem_pages (1296-1306). Reviewer round-15 claim (count_free_highmem_pages iterates zones under zone->lock) is WRONG: it uses for_each_populated_zone and zone_page_state(zone, NR_FREE_PAGES), which take no zone lock; the 'no locks, no allocation' statements stand for this function and that callee. The non-HIGHMEM stub returns 0 (2003). Prose otherwise correct, kept.

name: suspend_enter
prose: Precondition: devices have already been suspended and state is a supported sleep state, where suspend_ops (and suspend_ops->enter) is dereferenced only for states other than PM_SUSPEND_TO_IDLE, so it need only be non-NULL for those, and wakeup points to a valid bool. Postcondition: returns 0 on success (including the PM_SUSPEND_TO_IDLE path that runs s2idle_loop and the suspend_test(TEST_PLATFORM/TEST_CPUS/TEST_CORE) paths), or the negative errno of the first failing stage (platform_suspend_prepare, dpm_suspend_late, platform_suspend_prepare_late, dpm_suspend_noirq, platform_suspend_prepare_noirq, pm_sleep_disable_secondary_cpus, syscore_suspend or suspend_ops->enter), or -EBUSY when a wakeup is pending at the core stage; *wakeup is set to pm_wakeup_pending() only when syscore_suspend succeeds and is left unchanged otherwise; on failure only the stages already applied are undone, starting at the label matching the failed stage (an early failure runs just platform_resume_finish, later ones add dpm_resume_early, platform_resume_early, dpm_resume_noirq and platform_resume_noirq in reverse order), and once the core stage is reached system_state is restored to SYSTEM_RUNNING, IRQs are re-enabled and secondary CPUs are re-enabled before those resume callbacks.
note: Read suspend.c:412-491. Reviewer claims: round-2 (early failures only run platform_resume_finish) RIGHT and already in prose; round-15 (suspend_ops non-NULL is not required for PM_SUSPEND_TO_IDLE, which only calls s2idle_loop at 441-443) RIGHT; precondition corrected. Unwind labels verified: Platform_finish, Devices_early_resume, Platform_early_resume, Platform_wake, Enable_cpus.

name: load_compressed_image
prose: The caller passes a valid swap map handle, a valid snapshot handle, and nr_to_read, with swsusp_header valid and hib_comp_algo naming an available async compression algorithm. On success it returns 0 after all image pages have been read, decompressed, written through snapshot_write_next, finalized, and (when SF_CRC32_MODE is set) CRC32-checked; on failure it returns a negative error code (-ENOMEM, -EFAULT, -1, -ENODATA, or an error from swap_read_page, hib_wait_io, or snapshot_write_next) after stopping every started kthread and freeing all ring pages, acomp requests/contexts, and the data/crc structures, leaving the snapshot possibly partially written, and if snapshot_write_next returns a positive value and the loop ends because no more data is available it returns that positive value without finalizing; the caller retains ownership of handle and snapshot and receives no new references.
note: Packet name load_image_and_uncompress is not defined; real function is load_compressed_image at swap.c:1206-1536 (slice began inside it). Read it with its returns/gotos: -ENOMEM on page/data/crc/thread allocation failures, -EFAULT when crypto_alloc_acomp fails (1268), -1 for an invalid compressed or uncompressed length or short data at EOF, error values from swap_read_page, hib_wait_io, decompression and snapshot_write_next, -ENODATA from snapshot_write_finalize / not fully loaded / CRC32 mismatch; out_clean always stops the started kthreads and frees pages, acomp state and the data and crc structures; a positive snapshot_write_next value leaves out_finish without finalizing (1497). Prose correct, kept.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE4(ptrace, compat_long_t, request, compat_long_t, pid,
prose: Generated function compat_sys_ptrace(request, pid, addr, data). Precondition: request, pid, addr and data are the raw compat system-call arguments, with pid naming a virtual pid of the target task; no constraint is placed on their values. Postcondition: if request is PTRACE_TRACEME the function returns the result of ptrace_traceme() (0 or a negative errno) without ever taking a task reference; otherwise it looks the task up by vpid and returns -ESRCH if no such task exists; for PTRACE_ATTACH or PTRACE_SEIZE it returns the result of ptrace_attach() (0 or a negative errno); for every other request it first calls ptrace_check_attach() and returns its negative error if that fails, and otherwise returns the value of compat_arch_ptrace() (0, a negative errno, or a non-negative data word for peek-style requests), calling ptrace_unfreeze_traced() on the child unless that call succeeded with request equal to PTRACE_DETACH; on every path where find_get_task_by_vpid() obtained a task reference it is released with put_task_struct() before returning, so the caller holds no task reference and no ptrace lock.
note: Read ptrace.c:1542-1576. PTRACE_TRACEME returns ptrace_traceme() with no task reference (1548-1550); -ESRCH when find_get_task_by_vpid fails; PTRACE_ATTACH/SEIZE return ptrace_attach's result; otherwise ptrace_check_attach then compat_arch_ptrace, with ptrace_unfreeze_traced skipped only on success with PTRACE_DETACH (1568-1569); put_task_struct on all paths that obtained the child. Prose correct, kept.

name: rcu_segcblist_accelerate
prose: Precondition: rsclp points to an initialized rcu_segcblist (a WARN_ON_ONCE fires but execution continues if it is not enabled), seq is a grace-period sequence number, and the function takes no locks and acquires no references, so the caller retains ownership of rsclp. Postcondition: if segments RCU_WAIT_TAIL, RCU_NEXT_READY_TAIL and RCU_NEXT_TAIL are all empty, or if the highest-indexed non-empty segment among RCU_WAIT_TAIL and RCU_NEXT_READY_TAIL whose gp_seq is less than seq is RCU_NEXT_READY_TAIL, or if that segment is RCU_WAIT_TAIL and both RCU_NEXT_READY_TAIL and RCU_NEXT_TAIL are empty, the function returns false and leaves the segcblist unchanged; otherwise, letting k be the segment just above that highest-indexed segment (RCU_WAIT_TAIL if there is none, RCU_NEXT_READY_TAIL if it is RCU_WAIT_TAIL), it moves all callbacks from segments k+1 through RCU_NEXT_TAIL into segment k, sets gp_seq[k] through gp_seq[RCU_NEXT_READY_TAIL] to seq, empties segments k+1 through RCU_NEXT_TAIL, leaves segments RCU_DONE_TAIL through k-1 unchanged, and returns true.
note: Read rcu_segcblist.c:526-587 and rcu_segcblist_restempty/segempty (rcu_segcblist.h:103-117). Reviewer claims: round-1 and round-2 (false when all gp_seq >= seq) not applicable to this prose; round-15 (when WAIT/NEXT_READY/NEXT are all empty the function returns true because restempty is checked before the increment) is WRONG: restempty(DONE) at 531 returns false for that case; the 'only WAIT non-empty' case returns true only when that segment's gp_seq is not below seq (then i becomes WAIT_TAIL at 568), and returns false when it is below seq (restempty(WAIT) at 568), exactly as the prose states. Prose kept.
